The underlying metric is credit card spend. The array is the equally weighted arithmetic mean of its constituent year-over-year indices. At listing, its members are Urban Outfitters, American Eagle Outfitters, Abercrombie & Fitch, each weighted 1/3. Each constituent index is 100 when its measured credit card spend equals the same month of the previous year; the array averages these indices. An array level of 103 means the constituents' average year-over-year growth is 3%, and 97 means their average decline is 3%.

For example, the value for August is recorded at 11:59 p.m. ET on September 4. Later corrections or revisions will not affect the recorded value.

The reference is Carbon Arc's published full-month Gas Station Spend Array level: https://www.carbonarc.co/prisms?prism=4c7ec991-0913-4e7f-9fca-c525d44a483b&entity=Gas+Station+Spend. The underlying metric is credit card spend. The array is the equally weighted arithmetic mean of its constituent year-over-year indices. At listing, its members are ExxonMobil Corporation, BP (British Petroleum), Royal Dutch Shell, Chevron, each weighted 1/4. Each constituent index is 100 when its measured credit card spend equals the same month of the previous year; the array averages these indices. An array level of 103 means the constituents' average year-over-year growth is 3%, and 97 means their average decline is 3%.

markets.rules_primary: If the Carbon Arc Foot Locker Credit Card Spend (November 2026) for November 2026 is above 91, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
For purposes of this market, determination will resolve on finalized Carbon Arc values recorded at 11:59 p.m. ET on the 4th calendar day after the end of the month covered by this market. For example, finalized Carbon Arc values for August will be recorded at 11:59 p.m. ET on September 4th.

The index measures year-over-year change, where 100 means Foot Locker Credit Card Spend was equal to the same month last year. Values above 100 indicate growth and values below 100 indicate decline: for example, 103 = 3% more spend than year prior, 97 = 3% decline from year prior. The index is measured by Carbon Arc's aggregated U.S. credit and debit card transaction panel, matched to the same period of the prior year. The panel updates daily as new data arrives.

markets.rules_primary: If the Carbon Arc Fast food credit card spend array index (November 2026) for November 2026 is above 80, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
For purposes of this market, determination will resolve on the Carbon Arc Quick Service Restaurants Array value for the full month covered by this market, as recorded by Kalshi at 11:59 p.m. ET on the 4th calendar day after the end of that month. For example, the value for August is recorded at 11:59 p.m. ET on September 4th. Later corrections or revisions will not affect the recorded value. 

The reference is Carbon Arc's published full-month Quick Service Restaurants Array level: https://www.carbonarc.co/prisms?prism=e49b37cf-c5a9-4282-bba2-cd8c19c56a64. The array is the equally weighted arithmetic mean of its constituent year-over-year indices. At listing, its members are McDonald's, Starbucks, Chipotle, Wendy's and Chick-fil-A, weighted 20% each. Each constituent index is 100 when its measured value equals the same month of the previous year; the array averages these indices.

Kalshi is not affiliated, associated, authorized, endorsed by, or in any way officially connected with the underlying companies. All trademarks, logos, and brand names are the property of their respective owners.

The reference is Carbon Arc's published full-month Big Box Array level: https://www.carbonarc.co/prisms?prism=e7120baa-c555-4766-b1b7-99012347c8cd&entity=Big+Box. The underlying metric is credit card spend. The array is the equally weighted arithmetic mean of its constituent year-over-year indices. At listing, its members are Walmart Inc., Target, Best Buy Co, Costco Wholesale Corporation, each weighted 1/4. Each constituent index is 100 when its measured credit card spend equals the same month of the previous year; the array averages these indices. An array level of 103 means the constituents' average year-over-year growth is 3%, and 97 means their average decline is 3%.

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if the economic data is released.
markets.rules_primary: If the U.S. two-month net payroll revision published in the Bureau of Labor Statistics’ initial Employment Situation report covering November 2026 is above -100,000, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The underlying is the combined revision to the seasonally adjusted monthly changes in total nonfarm payroll employment for the two months immediately preceding November 2026, relative to their estimates in the immediately preceding Employment Situation release.

The two revisions will be added together, with upward revisions positive and downward revisions negative. Resolution will use the combined revision stated in the initial Employment Situation report covering November 2026; if no combined figure is stated, the two individual revisions will be summed.

Any benchmark or seasonal-adjustment effects incorporated into those two monthly revisions are included. Separate annual benchmark figures and revisions to other months are excluded.

Subsequent revisions will not affect the outcome.

markets.rules_primary: If core CPI inflation MoM is above headline CPI inflation MoM for November 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Only the first non-preliminary release of each value will be used. Revisions published after the first non-preliminary release will not affect resolution.

For purposes of this market, “core CPI” means the seasonally adjusted one-month percent change for “All items less food and energy” in the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers, as reported by BLS. “Headline CPI” means the seasonally adjusted one-month percent change for “All items” in the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers, as reported by BLS. The comparison will use the one-decimal values reported by BLS. If the values are equal, the market resolves No.

markets.rules_primary: If the Carbon Arc Zyn Point of Sale Growth (November 2026) for November 2026 is above 94.5 , then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
For purposes of this market, determination will resolve on finalized Carbon Arc values recorded at 11:59 p.m. ET on the 2nd calendar day after the end of the month covered by this market. For example, finalized Carbon Arc values for August will be recorded at 11:59 p.m. ET on September 2nd.

The index measures year-over-year change, where 100 means Zyn Point of Sale Growth was equal to the same month last year. Values above 100 indicate growth and values below 100 indicate decline: for example, 103 = 3% more spend than year prior, 97 = 3% decline from year prior. The index is measured by Carbon Arc's point-of-sale receipt panel using in-store and online purchases captured via receipt-scanning and rewards apps, matched to the same period of the prior year. The panel updates daily as new data arrives.

markets.rules_primary: If the Carbon Arc Mountain Dew Point of Sale Growth (November 2026) for November 2026 is above 101.5 , then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
For purposes of this market, determination will resolve on finalized Carbon Arc values recorded at 11:59 p.m. ET on the 2nd calendar day after the end of the month covered by this market. For example, finalized Carbon Arc values for August will be recorded at 11:59 p.m. ET on September 2nd.

The index measures year-over-year change, where 100 means Mountain Dew Point of Sale Growth was equal to the same month last year. Values above 100 indicate growth and values below 100 indicate decline: for example, 103 = 3% more spend than year prior, 97 = 3% decline from year prior. The index is measured by Carbon Arc's point-of-sale receipt panel using in-store and online purchases captured via receipt-scanning and rewards apps, matched to the same period of the prior year. The panel updates daily as new data arrives.

An array level of 103 means the constituents' average year-over-year growth is 3%, and 97 means their average decline is 3%.

markets.rules_secondary:
Observation: Uses the closing index level of the one-minute candle ending Dec 9, 2026 at 2:45pm EST: the S&P 500 value as of 2:44:59 PM EST on December 9, 2026, the preceding minute's final second. Each market compares that same observation with its stated fixed index-point strike. At least includes equality, which resolves Yes. The named economic event provides context; a delayed or rescheduled release does not automatically move the observation time.

Source Agencies (in priority order): S&P Dow Jones Indices, Pyth Network (official S&P 500 feeds), Bloomberg, WSJ, TradingView, Yahoo Finance, CNBC. If sources conflict, this order governs; any remaining dispute is resolved by Kalshi under Rule 7.1.

What counts as the S&P 500 value:
Only the index level calculated by S&P Dow Jones Indices, to two decimal places.
ETFs, futures, options, perpetuals, and constituent stock prices do not count.
If no time of day is specified, the official closing value for each trading day is used. Intraday, open, high/low, and pre-/after-hours values do not count.

Trading days:
Only days with an official S&P 500 close count (Eastern Time). Weekends and market holidays are ignored.
If the specified observation is at or after an early close or a halt ending trading for the day, the official close designated by S&P Dow Jones Indices governs.

Index changes:
Changes to constituents, weightings, divisor, or methodology do not affect the contract.
If the index is renamed, rebranded, or re-coded but its record continues, the contract stays open. If it is discontinued with no successor, the No-data rule applies.

No data:
If no Source Agency publishes a value by the Expiration Date (including if markets are closed for the entire period), all markets resolve No, unless a "No data" strike is listed, in which case that strike resolves Yes.

Corrections:
Corrections published before Expiration govern; corrections published after Expiration are ignored.
If Kalshi finds a material error, it may delay Expiration until a corrected value is published. If none is published by the Expiration Date, the No-data rule applies.

Observation precision: If the exact-second index level is unavailable, the same-minute precision permitted by the contract applies. A different-time or stale price is not an automatic substitute.

Kalshi is not affiliated, associated, authorized, endorsed by, or in any way officially connected with the S&P Dow Jones Indices. All trademarks, logos, and brand names are the property of their respective owners.

markets.rules_primary: If the value of the S&P 500 index, as calculated by S&P Dow Jones Indices, on December 9, 2026 at 2:44:59 PM EST is at least 7225.00, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Observation: Uses the closing index level of the one-minute candle ending Dec 9, 2026 at 2:45pm EST: the S&P 500 value as of 2:44:59 PM EST on December 9, 2026, the preceding minute's final second. Each market compares that same observation with its stated fixed index-point strike. At least includes equality, which resolves Yes. The named economic event provides context; a delayed or rescheduled release does not automatically move the observation time.

Source Agencies (in priority order): S&P Dow Jones Indices, Pyth Network (official S&P 500 feeds), Bloomberg, WSJ, TradingView, Yahoo Finance, CNBC. If sources conflict, this order governs; any remaining dispute is resolved by Kalshi under Rule 7.1.

What counts as the S&P 500 value:
Only the index level calculated by S&P Dow Jones Indices, to two decimal places.
ETFs, futures, options, perpetuals, and constituent stock prices do not count.
If no time of day is specified, the official closing value for each trading day is used. Intraday, open, high/low, and pre-/after-hours values do not count.

Trading days:
Only days with an official S&P 500 close count (Eastern Time). Weekends and market holidays are ignored.
If the specified observation is at or after an early close or a halt ending trading for the day, the official close designated by S&P Dow Jones Indices governs.

Index changes:
Changes to constituents, weightings, divisor, or methodology do not affect the contract.
If the index is renamed, rebranded, or re-coded but its record continues, the contract stays open. If it is discontinued with no successor, the No-data rule applies.

No data:
If no Source Agency publishes a value by the Expiration Date (including if markets are closed for the entire period), all markets resolve No, unless a "No data" strike is listed, in which case that strike resolves Yes.

Corrections:
Corrections published before Expiration govern; corrections published after Expiration are ignored.
If Kalshi finds a material error, it may delay Expiration until a corrected value is published. If none is published by the Expiration Date, the No-data rule applies.

Observation precision: If the exact-second index level is unavailable, the same-minute precision permitted by the contract applies. A different-time or stale price is not an automatic substitute.

Kalshi is not affiliated, associated, authorized, endorsed by, or in any way officially connected with the S&P Dow Jones Indices. All trademarks, logos, and brand names are the property of their respective owners.

If no time of day is specified, the official closing value for each trading day is used. Intraday, open, high/low, and pre-/after-hours values do not count.

Trading days:
Only days with an official S&P 500 close count (Eastern Time). Weekends and market holidays are ignored.
If the specified observation is at or after an early close or a halt ending trading for the day, the official close designated by S&P Dow Jones Indices governs.

Index changes:
Changes to constituents, weightings, divisor, or methodology do not affect the contract.
If the index is renamed, rebranded, or re-coded but its record continues, the contract stays open. If it is discontinued with no successor, the No-data rule applies.

No data:
If no Source Agency publishes a value by the Expiration Date (including if markets are closed for the entire period), all markets resolve No, unless a "No data" strike is listed, in which case that strike resolves Yes.

Corrections:
Corrections published before Expiration govern; corrections published after Expiration are ignored.
If Kalshi finds a material error, it may delay Expiration until a corrected value is published. If none is published by the Expiration Date, the No-data rule applies.

Observation precision: If the exact-second index level is unavailable, the same-minute precision permitted by the contract applies. A different-time or stale price is not an automatic substitute.

markets.rules_secondary:
Observation: Uses the closing index level of the one-minute candle ending Dec 9, 2026 at 2:15pm EST: the S&P 500 value as of 2:14:59 PM EST on December 9, 2026, the preceding minute's final second. Each market compares that same observation with its stated fixed index-point strike. At least includes equality, which resolves Yes. The named economic event provides context; a delayed or rescheduled release does not automatically move the observation time.

Source Agencies (in priority order): S&P Dow Jones Indices, Pyth Network (official S&P 500 feeds), Bloomberg, WSJ, TradingView, Yahoo Finance, CNBC. If sources conflict, this order governs; any remaining dispute is resolved by Kalshi under Rule 7.1.

What counts as the S&P 500 value:
Only the index level calculated by S&P Dow Jones Indices, to two decimal places.
ETFs, futures, options, perpetuals, and constituent stock prices do not count.
If no time of day is specified, the official closing value for each trading day is used. Intraday, open, high/low, and pre-/after-hours values do not count.

Trading days:
Only days with an official S&P 500 close count (Eastern Time). Weekends and market holidays are ignored.
If the specified observation is at or after an early close or a halt ending trading for the day, the official close designated by S&P Dow Jones Indices governs.

Index changes:
Changes to constituents, weightings, divisor, or methodology do not affect the contract.
If the index is renamed, rebranded, or re-coded but its record continues, the contract stays open. If it is discontinued with no successor, the No-data rule applies.

No data:
If no Source Agency publishes a value by the Expiration Date (including if markets are closed for the entire period), all markets resolve No, unless a "No data" strike is listed, in which case that strike resolves Yes.

Corrections:
Corrections published before Expiration govern; corrections published after Expiration are ignored.
If Kalshi finds a material error, it may delay Expiration until a corrected value is published. If none is published by the Expiration Date, the No-data rule applies.

Observation precision: If the exact-second index level is unavailable, the same-minute precision permitted by the contract applies. A different-time or stale price is not an automatic substitute.

Kalshi is not affiliated, associated, authorized, endorsed by, or in any way officially connected with the S&P Dow Jones Indices. All trademarks, logos, and brand names are the property of their respective owners.

markets.rules_secondary:
Observation: Uses the closing index level of the one-minute candle ending Dec 9, 2026 at 2:15pm EST: the S&P 500 value as of 2:14:59 PM EST on December 9, 2026, the preceding minute's final second. Each market compares that same observation with its stated fixed index-point strike. At least includes equality, which resolves Yes. The named economic event provides context; a delayed or rescheduled release does not automatically move the observation time.

Source Agencies (in priority order): S&P Dow Jones Indices, Pyth Network (official S&P 500 feeds), Bloomberg, WSJ, TradingView, Yahoo Finance, CNBC. If sources conflict, this order governs; any remaining dispute is resolved by Kalshi under Rule 7.1.

What counts as the S&P 500 value:
Only the index level calculated by S&P Dow Jones Indices, to two decimal places.
ETFs, futures, options, perpetuals, and constituent stock prices do not count.
If no time of day is specified, the official closing value for each trading day is used. Intraday, open, high/low, and pre-/after-hours values do not count.

Trading days:
Only days with an official S&P 500 close count (Eastern Time). Weekends and market holidays are ignored.
If the specified observation is at or after an early close or a halt ending trading for the day, the official close designated by S&P Dow Jones Indices governs.

Index changes:
Changes to constituents, weightings, divisor, or methodology do not affect the contract.
If the index is renamed, rebranded, or re-coded but its record continues, the contract stays open. If it is discontinued with no successor, the No-data rule applies.

No data:
If no Source Agency publishes a value by the Expiration Date (including if markets are closed for the entire period), all markets resolve No, unless a "No data" strike is listed, in which case that strike resolves Yes.

Corrections:
Corrections published before Expiration govern; corrections published after Expiration are ignored.
If Kalshi finds a material error, it may delay Expiration until a corrected value is published. If none is published by the Expiration Date, the No-data rule applies.

Observation precision: If the exact-second index level is unavailable, the same-minute precision permitted by the contract applies. A different-time or stale price is not an automatic substitute.

Kalshi is not affiliated, associated, authorized, endorsed by, or in any way officially connected with the S&P Dow Jones Indices. All trademarks, logos, and brand names are the property of their respective owners.
